title: Copied code, measured
headline: Copied code is not where this codebase's bloat is, and that holds after a third look: 1.0% of non-test code is an exact copy (4,803 of 472,586 lines) and 4.75% a near-copy with every name and literal normalised; unit and integration tests (1.8% and 3.2%) and the e2e folder (1.7% and 7.4%) are no worse. The fourteen checked findings are true duplicates or missing checks, none rests on a feature being unused, and their corrected savings add up to about 5,500 lines (1.2%); my two additions are small too: about 1,100 to 1,500 test lines of repeated scaffolding (448 integration tests stub a module the test config already stubs) and helpers re-solved under one name (addDays in 10 files, countryName exported from 6 with three different answers for a missing code). Do first, because they are small and safe: one store-address helper for the 27 hand-written lookups behind production's most-called statement (560,090 calls with no shoppers), and a copy ratchet in CI. Do before opening, while every table holds only test rows: one import definition, one engine with a scope for the platform's workflows and deliveries, and one Work view for store and account.

findings.title: A store's address by its id is looked up by hand in 27 places beside a cached helper that already exists; it is production's most-called statement
findings.evidence: rg finds `select slug from commerce.stores where id = ...` written out 27 times in 21 server files (custom-fields.ts five times); 25 are exactly the statement that tops production's call list: 560,090 calls in 78 days, about 5 a minute, with no shoppers (prod-db-stats.md:86). The usual next line is the cached getStore(slug). A cached helper exists: storeSlugOf() in menus.ts:282 ('use cache', cacheLife days, 12 callers). storeOf() in product-data.ts:27 does the same uncached. storeAndMarket() (content-grid.ts:151) makes the lookup uncached on storefront sections. The earlier checks said no code rewrites a store's slug. That is not quite so: commerce.adopt_sandbox() sets a new slug when a sandbox is kept (baseline_1_schema.sql:786-790, called from platform.ts:388), and the trigger stores_sandbox_rules() lets only that function move a sandbox's address (:19349). Nothing in src or the migrations rewrites the slug of a store that is not a sandbox, but no database rule forbids it. adoptRequestSandbox() marks the store's two tags stale (platform.ts:396-397); storeSlugOf()'s entry has no tag and lives for days. Wider than the slug, by my count: 152 single-row reads of commerce.stores by id in 102 server files with about 30 column lists (time_zone 13 times in 10 files); forms.ts:57-60 loads the store and then reads its time zone with a second query. Most of the others are admin writes that need a fresh value and should stay. Which callers make the 560,090 calls was not measured.
findings.cost: One database round trip each time code knows a store by its id; today about 7,200 a day from builds, crawlers, scheduled work and the team's testing. On storefront sections it is paid per uncached render, so it grows with shoppers and with stores.
findings.who_pays: The database and the server, per render and per scheduled run.
fix_steps: 1. src/server/stores.ts: move the cached reader here from src/server/menus.ts:281-287, keep 'use cache' and cacheLife('days') so prerendered callers stay cacheable, make it select slug and sandbox, and give it a tag by id (cacheTag of a new storeIdTag(id)). Put a module-level Map<string, string> in front of it: storeSlugById(id) answers from the Map, else asks the cached reader and remembers the slug only when the store is not a sandbox. Never remember a miss.

1b. src/server/platform.ts:396-397 (adoptRequestSandbox): mark storeIdTag(storeId) stale beside the two store tags it already marks, so the kept store's new address is read again. This also closes today's gap in storeSlugOf().

1c. findings.evidence: My count: 284 top-level input, field, control, card, label and hint class constants in 171 admin files (the second check counted 376 with th, td, primary and secondary and files outside the admin; input alone has 15 spellings, field 20). The kit (ui/index.ts) exports Button, Chip, Card, bars, List, PageHeader and FocusFrame: no input, select, table or skeleton. data/ui.ts already shares field, label, hint, a table shell, th and td, for the data pages only. findings.who_pays: Owners (controls that look and behave slightly differently per screen) and agents (a new screen copies a neighbour's constants). The build pays almost nothing.
